2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)](#project-structure-from-uip-maestro-flow-init)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
44	
45	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
46	
47	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by `uip maestro flow init` and packaging. Do not add them manually.
48	
49	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
50	
51	## Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)
52	
53	```
54	<ProjectName>/
55	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
56	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
57	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
58	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
59	├── operate.json            # runtime options
60	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
61	```
62	
63	## Node instance
64	
65	```json
66	{
67	  "id": "rollDice",
68	  "type": "core.action.script",
69	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
70	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
71	  "inputs": {
72	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
73	  },
74	  "outputs": {
75	    "output": {
76	      "type": "object",
77	      "description": "The return value of the script",
78	      "source": "=result.response",
79	      "var": "output"
80	    },
81	    "error": {
82	      "type": "object",
83	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
84	      "source": "=result.Error",
85	      "var": "error"
86	    }
87	  }
88	}
89	```
90	
91	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
92	
93	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
94	
95	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
96	>
97	> ```
98	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
99	> ```
100	>
101	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
102	
103	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
104	>
105	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.

113	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |

For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
116	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |

1	# Connections
2	
3	Connections are authenticated sessions for a specific connector. They store credentials and tokens, and can be shared across automations within a folder.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Response Fields
10	
11	| Field | Show to user? | Description |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| **`Name`** | **Yes** | Display name — always use this as the primary identifier when presenting to the user (e.g., "Salesforce Prod", "bai.li") |
14	| **`State`** | **Yes** | `Enabled` or other status. Only Enabled connections can be used. |
15	| **`IsDefault`** | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. Recommend the default connection but always let the user confirm. |
16	| **`Owner`** | **Yes** | Who created the connection (email) |
17	| **`Folder`** | **Yes** | Folder name this connection belongs to (e.g., "Shared", "Personal") |
18	| `ConnectorName` | **Yes** | Human-readable connector name (e.g., "Slack", "Salesforce") |
19	| `ByoaConnection` | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connection — customer registered their own OAuth app with the external service. Required for some webhook triggers. |
20	| `Id` | Internal | Connection UUID — use only in `--connection-id` CLI args, never show to user |
21	| `ConnectorKey` | Internal | Connector key — use only in CLI args |
22	| `FolderKey` | Internal | Folder UUID — use only in `--folder-key` CLI args, never show to user |
23	| `ElementInstanceId` | Internal | Numeric instance ID — use only in `--element-instance-id` for `uip is webhooks config` |
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Command Syntax
28	
29	`<connector-key>` is a **positional argument**, not a flag:
30	
31	```bash
32	# Correct — always pass --all-folders for discovery (see Folder Scoping below)
33	uip is connections list "uipath-salesforce-slack" --all-folders --output json
34	
35	# WRONG — there is no --connector-key flag
36	uip is connections list --connector-key "uipath-salesforce-slack"
37	```
38	
39	**Always pass a connector key.** Running `uip is connections list` with no arg returns a noisy, paginated list across every connector in the tenant and is not a useful survey step.
40	
41	**Wrong key?** If the call errors with "connector not found" or returns empty unexpectedly, look up the correct key:
42	
43	```bash
44	uip is connectors list --filter "<vendor>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	Connector keys are prefixed by source — `uipath-<vendor>-<service>` for catalog connectors, `custom-entity-*` for tenant-built. See [connectors.md — Connector Disambiguation](connectors.md#connector-disambiguation) for the full classification ladder.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Selecting a Connection
52	
53	### Connector-Specific Overrides
54	
55	**Before applying the auto-select rule below, check this table.** If the connector key (and node-type pattern, where listed) matches an entry, read the linked file and follow its rules. Override supersedes the auto-select rule.
56	
57	| Connector key | Applies when | Override action | Detail |
58	|---|---|---|---|
59	| `uipath-microsoft-teams` | `send-bot-*` activity node types | Ask user; warn that bot scope is required | [uipath-microsoft-teams.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-microsoft-teams.md#connection-selection-override) |
60	| `uipath-salesforce-slack` | Webhook trigger node types (allow-list — excludes `button-clicked`) | Ask user; filter `--byoa` from the start | [uipath-salesforce-slack.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-salesforce-slack.md#connection-selection-override) |
61	
62	To add a new override, see [connector-overrides/README.md](connector-overrides/README.md).
63	
64	---
65	
66	**Auto-select rule (no prompt) — when all three hold:**
67	
68	- `IsDefault: Yes`
69	- `State: Enabled`
70	- `Folder` is the user's personal workspace
71	
72	Bind silently and skip the presentation steps below.
73	
74	Detect the user's personal workspace once per session — list all folders and filter for the personal type:
75	
76	```bash
77	uip or folders list --all --output json
78	# → Data: [{ Name, Key, Path, Description, Type, ParentKey }]
79	# Filter entries where Type == "Personal"
80	```
81	
82	Match `connection.FolderKey` against the personal workspace's `Key`. If the call returns multiple personal workspaces (admin tenant) or no match, fall through to the presentation flow.
83	
84	**Otherwise — present connections to the user.** Recommend the default but let the user confirm.
85	
86	### Folder Scoping (`--all-folders`)
87	
88	**Always pass `--all-folders` when discovering connections.** Without it, the CLI returns the active folder only — producing false "no connections found" results when the connection exists in another folder you can see. After the user picks a connection, capture its `FolderKey` from the response for downstream binding; do not pass `--folder-key` during discovery.
89	
90	- `--all-folders`: spans every folder you have access to. Works with or without a `<connector-key>` positional.
91	- **Mutually exclusive with `--folder` / `--folder-key`** — passing both fails with `Result: Failure`, `Message: "Conflicting folder flags..."`, exit code 1.
92	
93	### For Native Connectors
94	
95	1. List connections for the connector across all folders:
96	
97	   ```bash
98	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
99	   ```
100	
101	2. Present all enabled connections to the user using **Name, Owner, and Folder** (never UUIDs), **recommending** the default (`IsDefault: Yes`, `State: Enabled`):
102	   - "I found these connections: 1) **Salesforce Prod** by user@example.com (default, enabled, Shared folder) ← recommended 2) **Salesforce Dev** by admin@example.com (enabled, Shared folder). Which should I use?"
103	3. If only one enabled connection exists, still confirm: "I found connection **<Name>** by <Owner> in **<Folder>** folder (default, enabled). Should I use this one?"
104	4. **Verify health — ping after every selection** (auto-select and user-confirmed alike):
105	
106	   ```bash
107	   uip is connections ping "<connection-id>" --output json
108	   ```
109	
110	   If ping fails or reports not Enabled, follow step 5.
111	
112	5. If not enabled (from list `State` or ping result) → prompt user to re-authenticate via `is connections edit <id>`, then re-ping.
113	
114	6. **No connections in step 1 — bypass the cache before concluding none exist:**
115	   1. Retry with `--refresh`:
116	      ```bash
117	      uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --refresh --output json
118	      ```
119	   2. If still empty, prompt user to create one via `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`.
120	
121	### For BYOA Connections (Webhook Triggers)
122	
123	BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connections use an OAuth app the customer registered with the external service (e.g., a Slack app they own). Some webhook triggers require BYOA; many do not. **The requirement is per event object, not per connector** — read it from the `triggers objects` response.
124	
125	**Decision flow:**
126	
127	1. Get any enabled connection — needed only as `--connection-id` for the next call:
128	
129	   ```bash
130	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
131	   ```
132	
133	2. Query trigger objects and read the `byoaConnection` flag for the matching event:
134	
135	   ```bash
136	   uip is triggers objects "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" \
137	     --connection-id "<id>" --output json
138	   ```
139	
140	3. **If `byoaConnection: true`** — the connection from step 1 is not usable. Filter to BYOA across all folders:
141	
142	   ```bash
143	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --output json
144	   ```
145	
146	   If empty, retry with `--refresh` to bypass the CLI cache:
147	
148	   ```bash
149	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --refresh --output json
150	   ```
151	
152	   If still empty, **stop and tell the user**: "This trigger requires a BYOA connection for `<connector-key>`. None found. Create one in the Integration Service portal or with `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`, then re-run."
153	
154	4. **If `byoaConnection: false`** — use the connection from step 1. Verify health with `uip is connections ping "<id>" --output json`.
155	
156	> Connector-specific OAuth-app setup instructions (e.g., what permissions a Slack app needs) come from the trigger's `design.textBlocks` field in the `triggers objects` response. Surface that text to the user verbatim — do not invent service-specific guidance.
157	
158	For webhook URL retrieval after the trigger is configured, see [triggers.md — Webhook URL Retrieval](triggers.md#webhook-url-retrieval).
159	
160	### For HTTP Fallback
161	
162	1. List connections for `uipath-uipath-http`
163	2. Look for a connection whose **Name** contains the target vendor (case-insensitive substring match, e.g., "Apify" matches "Apify", "Apify - Prod", "My Apify Connection")
164	3. Present matches to the user. If multiple matches → let them choose.
165	4. If no match → present all existing HTTP connections and ask the user to choose, or offer to create a new one
166	
167	> **Note:** Name-based matching is best-effort. If connection names don't follow vendor naming conventions, present all HTTP connections to the user.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Folder Scoping
172	
173	`uip is connections list <connector-key>` defaults to filtering by the **current** folder context — results from other folders (including the user's personal workspace) are silently excluded. Empty response on the filtered side looks like:
174	
175	```json
176	{"Message":"No connections found for connector '<connector-key>'."}
177	```
178	
179	even though a connection exists in another folder.
180	
181	**Cross-folder pattern** — pass `--folder` explicitly:
182	
183	```bash
184	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
185	```
186	
187	**Enumerate every folder** — iterate folders and list per folder:
188	
189	```bash
190	uip or folders list --output json
191	# → for each folder, call:
192	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
193	```
194	
195	> If the user reports "connection exists in my personal workspace but CLI can't see it", suspect default folder filtering — re-list with `--folder` set to that workspace before creating a new connection.
196	
197	---
198	
199	## Identifying a JDBC Connection's Target DB
200	
201	For the JDBC gateway connector (`uipath-uipath-jdbc`, "Database Hub"), `connections list` does **not** expose `jdbcUrl` or `driverClass` — config is intentionally hidden. The only signal for "what DB does this JDBC connection point to?" is the connection **`name`**.
202	
203	Match case-insensitively (weak signal — surface as "likely <DB>", never "is <DB>"):
204	
205	| DB | Substrings in `connection.name` |
206	|---|---|
207	| Snowflake | `snowflake`, `sf` |
208	| Databricks | `databricks`, `dbx` |
209	| Postgres | `postgres`, `postgresql`, `pg` |
210	| MySQL | `mysql` |
211	| SQL Server | `sqlserver`, `mssql` |
212	| Oracle | `oracle` |
213	| Redshift | `redshift` |
214	| BigQuery | `bigquery`, `bq` |
215	
216	If the user explicitly named a connection in their prompt (e.g. "use the `pat_databricks` connection"), that overrides name-matching — bind it directly.
217	
218	Used by the [connectors.md — JDBC Gateway](connectors.md#jdbc-gateway--database-sql-intent) decision matrix.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## Getting a Connection's Vendor Base URL
223	
224	`uip is connections base-url <connection-id>` returns the exact vendor base URL the connection uses for proxied calls (e.g., raw `http-request` calls, Managed HTTP Request in connector mode). Manual-mode invocations don't use it. The connection must be Enabled.
225	
226	```bash
227	uip is connections base-url "<connection-id>" --output json
228	# → { "Result": "Success", "Code": "ConnectionBaseUrl",
229	#     "Data": { "ConnectionId": "<id>", "BaseUrl": "https://..." } }
230	```
231	
232	Examples across connectors:
233	
234	| Connector | Returned `BaseUrl` |
235	|---|---|
236	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<site-id>/rest/api/2` |
237	| `uipath-microsoft-outlook365` | `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0` |
238	| `uipath-uipath-marketo` | `https://<account>.mktorest.com/rest` |
239	
240	Use this whenever you need to compose a relative `url` for `http-request` or Managed HTTP Request in connector mode. See [http-request.md](http-request.md).
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Scope-Related Errors
245	
246	A connection can be `Enabled` but lack optional OAuth scopes needed for specific activities. This typically surfaces as a **403 Forbidden** error during execute.
247	
248	**Symptoms:**
249	- Connection pings successfully (`State: Enabled`)
250	- Execute fails with 403 or a vendor-specific "insufficient permissions" error
251	- The same operation works with a different connection that has broader scopes
252	
253	**Recovery:**
254	1. Inform the user that the connection may need broader OAuth scopes for this activity
255	2. Re-authorize with broader scopes: `uip is connections edit <connection-id>`
256	3. After re-auth, ping again to verify, then retry the operation

1	# Resources
2	
3	Resources represent the data objects available through a connector (e.g., Salesforce Account, Contact, Opportunity). Each resource supports a set of CRUD operations.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	## Contents
8	- Listing and Describing Resources
9	- Response Fields
10	- Describe Response
11	- Describe Failures
12	- Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
13	- Execute Operations
14	- Pagination
15	- Execute Error Handling
16	
17	For reference field resolution (simple refs, dependency chains, required field validation), see [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md).
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Listing and Describing Resources
22	
23	**Always pass `--connection-id`** to get connection-specific metadata including custom objects and fields. Without it, only standard objects/fields are returned.
24	
25	## Response Fields
26	
27	| Field | Description |
28	|---|---|
29	| **`Name`** | Resource identifier (used in commands) |
30	| `DisplayName` | Human-readable name |
31	| `Path` | API path for this resource |
32	| `Type` | Resource type (standard, custom) |
33	| `SubType` | Sub-type (e.g., method, entity) |
34	
35	## Describe Response
36	
37	The describe command returns metadata from the raw API. The output depends on whether `--operation` is provided.
38	
39	### Without `--operation` — operation summary
40	
41	Returns which operations the resource supports:
42	
43	| Field | Description |
44	|---|---|
45	| **`availableOperations`** | List of operations — each with `method` (GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE), `name` (Create/List/etc.), `description`, `curated` (display name) |
46	| **`hint`** | Instructs to use `--operation` for field details |
47	
48	### With `--operation` — per-operation field detail
49	
50	Returns the full field breakdown for the specified operation:
51	
52	| Field | Description |
53	|---|---|
54	| **`operation`** | Operation info — `method`, `name`, `description`, `path`, `curated` display name |
55	| **`parameters`** | Path and query parameters (NOT body fields) — each with `name`, `type` (path/query), `dataType`, `required`, `defaultValue`, `reference` |
56	| **`requestFields`** | Fields to send in `--body` — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName`, `required`, `description`, `reference`, `enum` |
57	| **`responseFields`** | Fields returned in the response — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName` |
58	
59	> **Always use `--operation`** to get actionable field detail. Without it you only see which operations exist.
60	
61	### Key field properties
62	
63	- **`required: true`** — field must be provided in `--body` or `--query`. Do NOT skip.
64	- **`reference`** — field value must be looked up from another resource. See [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md). When baking a static value for a reference field, also emit `designTimeMetadata.designTimeLookups` so the edit-UI renders a label — see [reference-resolution.md — Static Reference-Value Labeling](reference-resolution.md#static-reference-value-labeling).
65	- **`enum`** — field only accepts the listed values (e.g., `["low", "normal", "high"]`).
66	
67	Results are cached locally. Use `--refresh` to bypass cache after re-auth or schema changes.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Describe Failures
72	
73	Some resources return an error on describe. This is a **server-side metadata gap** — do not retry with `--refresh`.
74	
75	**Recovery:**
76	
77	1. **Skip describe entirely** — do not waste calls retrying.
78	2. **Infer fields from user context** — use the field names and values the user provided in their request.
79	3. **Infer reference fields from naming** — see [reference-resolution.md — Inferring References Without Describe](reference-resolution.md#inferring-references-without-describe).
80	4. **Attempt execute directly** — let the server validate. If a field is rejected, read the error and adjust.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
85	
86	For connectors whose required fields depend on parent-field selections (Jira `GenerateSchema` keyed off project + issue type, Salesforce SOQL `GenerateQuerySchema` keyed off the query string, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant` keyed off `tenantEntityName`), the base `describe` returns only base fields. To preview the full required-field set the runtime will see, pass parent values via `-f, --field`:
87	
88	```bash
89	# Jira: project + issue type → custom fields (GET, query-param tokens)
90	uip is resources describe uipath-atlassian-jira curated_create_issue \
91	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
92	  -f fields.project.key=ENGCE \
93	  -f fields.issuetype.id=3 \
94	  --output json
95	
96	# Salesforce SOQL: query string → response columns (POST, body token)
97	uip is resources describe uipath-salesforce-sfdc query_records \
